title: Checkout errors spiking after Friday deploy
symptoms: Checkout requests failing with database connection errors; p99 latency 4.9s, error rate 25%, starting about 10 minutes after the v2.6.0 Friday deploy.
error_message: org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections
log_snippet:
2026-09-11T15:02:00Z ERROR payments-api [pool-2] org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections
p99_latency=4910ms error_rate=25.0% deploy=v2.6.0 (10 min ago)
notes: Recall should surface all 4 prior postgres_pool_exhaustion incidents on payments-api with dates and IDs -- the canonical 'incident 5 cites the past fix' demo moment.

title: Checkout errors again after the next Friday deploy
symptoms: Same connection-pool-exhaustion signature as the prior four incidents; on-call is about to try rolling back the deploy.
error_message: org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections
log_snippet:
2026-09-18T14:47:00Z ERROR payments-api [pool-2] org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections
p99_latency=4780ms error_rate=23.9% deploy=v2.6.1 (7 min ago)
notes: Recall's fix_attempts show rollback_to_previous_deploy failed on INC-002 and INC-017 (2 of 2 attempts) and increase_postgres_pool_size worked 4 of 4 times -- the agent should explicitly warn against rollback before it's tried.

title: Redis OOM on order-worker, Monday morning
symptoms: order-worker queue depth climbing and Redis OOM errors, Monday morning, matching the historical pattern.
error_message: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'.
log_snippet:
2026-09-14T07:10:00Z ERROR order-worker [redis-client] OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'.
redis_used_memory_pct=99.8% queue_depth=39210 maxmemory_policy=allkeys-lru
notes: reflect should surface 'order-worker Redis OOM recurred on 3 consecutive Mondays (May-July) and was root-caused/fixed in INC-015 (TTL key-prefix mismatch)' -- a reappearance after that fix is a notable, non-obvious insight, not just a repeat match.

title: Kafka consumer lag during Diwali Dhamaka Sale
symptoms: order-events consumer lag climbing fast within minutes of the Diwali Dhamaka Sale flash promotion starting.
error_message: consumer lag detected on order-processing consumer group
log_snippet:
2026-09-16T11:30:00Z WARN order-worker [kafka-consumer-group=order-processing] consumer lag detected partition=2 lag=22040 messages
throughput_msgs_sec=610 target_msgs_sec=1550 topic=order-events
notes: Rahul Mehta resolved both prior Kafka-lag-during-sale incidents; the briefing should suggest looping him in.
